title: what counts as "the query" for notebook recall
summary: The text the recall matcher scores is NOT what the user typed — every host wraps the user's words in editor and subagent telemetry (open file, current selection, a finished subagent's summary, a slash-command expansion), and that wrapper is file- and symbol-rich, so it reaches the matcher as if the user had named those files. The damage is concentrated in one place: the path-name override in search.ts tests substring containment of an anchor path against the WHOLE raw prompt and, on a match, sets strong/rare/strongTerms and +100, which its own comment describes as bypassing the term-rarity eligibility gate and the suppression gate. A stale-open editor tab therefore hijacks recall for consecutive turns (observed on a second machine: three straight turns about a global CLAUDE.md pulled a note about an unrelated custom-functions file). Fixed 2026-07-29 in the HOOKS, never in search.ts — the override is opts.strongOnly-gated, so tool-mode `kb search` must keep trusting a path the user typed literally. Incidence is environment-dependent: dominant on a 117-note work repo, only 4/238 here, which is why local analysis never saw it.

summary: The text the recall matcher scores is NOT what the user typed. Two distinct feeds prove it. (1) Every host wraps the user's words in editor/subagent telemetry, which is file- and symbol-rich and hijacks the path-name override in search.ts (+100, bypassing the rarity and suppression gates) — fixed 2026-07-29 in the HOOKS via recall-query.mjs, never in search.ts, because the override is opts.strongOnly-gated and tool-mode kb search must keep trusting a path the user typed literally. (2) OBSERVED 2026-07-29 in inject-log.jsonl: the PostToolUse nudge path also drives kb search --hook, so an AGENT's raw grep pattern lands in the log as a query and can inject — the record at 17:01:29Z has query 'rareCount |let rare = false' (a shell grep pattern, not a prompt) with implant:true against hooks-capture-payload-mjs. So an agent-term recall channel already exists in partial form; anyone measuring 'should we add grep terms as a signal' must subtract what the nudge already does.
